summary: 1. Start hooks with immediate, second-person direct actions or states about the viewer's body or daily life (e.g., 'Your eyes are leaking right now') rather than passive setup statements. 2. Keep titles concise and intrigue-focused without relies on heavy emoji filler or overly broad questions. 3. Eliminate scenario-building setups like 'Your car swerves off...' which cause immediate swiping (>70% drop-off). 4. Focus topics on universal human/everyday phenomena over niche infrastructure or passive historical trivia. 5. State the provocative core conflict in the very first 4 words of the spoken audio.
winning_hooks: Direct personal confrontation: Using 'Your' + present bodily/everyday state ('Your eyes are leaking right now')
Subverting obvious assumptions in under 8 words ('You are not sad when you chop an onion')
Short, punchy title framing that clearly states a relatable mystery ('Why your eyes are secretly leaking')
avoid: Hypothetical scenario setups that delay the core topic ('Your car swerves off the highway right toward...')
Generic background preamble ('Fossilized bones can last millions of years, but sometimes...')
Abstract or passive environmental topics that viewers do not feel personally connected to in the first 2 seconds (e.g., backyard pond freezing dynamics)
next_experiment: Test scenario-building vs. direct personal impact on the same topic: A) 'Your car swerves off the highway toward a steel wall...' vs B) 'Your car's guardrail is engineered to crumple like paper to save your life.'
